topic: Vasculitis and other Conditions Associated with Hematuria
stemEn: A child presented with hemoptysis and hematuria. Laboratory testing showed positive anti-GBM antibodies and negative pANCA antibodies. What is the most likely cause?
explanationAr: وجود pulmonary-renal syndrome مع hemoptysis + hematuria وpositive anti-GBM antibodies يجعل Anti-GBM disease هو مفتاح المصدر. سلبية pANCA تجعل ANCA-associated vasculitis أقل احتمالًا في صياغة السؤال.
reasoningEn: The combination of pulmonary hemorrhagic symptoms, glomerular hematuria, and positive anti-GBM antibodies supports anti-GBM disease.
incorrectOptionsAr: GPA غالبًا يرتبط PR3/cANCA أو MPO/pANCA مع upper-airway features. Alport يسبب hereditary hematuria مع hearing/ocular findings وليس anti-GBM antibody positivity. Lupus nephritis يحتاج SLE serology/clinical context.
clinicalPearl: Anti-GBM disease can present as a pulmonary-renal syndrome with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage.
diagnosticSteps: Urgent nephrology/rheumatology evaluation when pulmonary-renal syndrome is suspected

topic: Vasculitis and other Conditions Associated with Hematuria
stemEn: A child presented with recurrent sinusitis. Laboratory testing was positive for anti-proteinase-3 ANCA. What is the most likely cause?
explanationAr: Recurrent upper-airway disease مع PR3-ANCA/cANCA هو النمط الكلاسيكي في المصدر لـgranulomatosis with polyangiitis، والتي قد تصيب upper/lower respiratory tract والكلى.
reasoningEn: PR3-ANCA positivity plus recurrent sinus disease strongly supports granulomatosis with polyangiitis in the source.
incorrectOptionsAr: Sarcoidosis قد يسبب pulmonary/systemic disease لكنه لا يرتبط بشكل نموذجي بـPR3-ANCA ولا بهذا pattern من necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis.
clinicalPearl: GPA commonly involves upper airway, lungs, and kidneys and is often PR3-ANCA positive.

topic: Vasculitis and other Conditions Associated with Hematuria
stemEn: A 4-year-old boy presented with palpable bruises over his buttocks and lower extremities. He also complains of ankle and abdominal pain, consistent with Henoch-Schonlein purpura (IgA vasculitis). What is the most likely underlying pathology?
explanationAr: الـIgA vasculitis تتميز بـsmall-vessel leukocytoclastic vasculitis، ومع biopsy يظهر IgA deposition في postcapillary venules. وجود palpable purpura في HSP ليس بسبب thrombocytopenia.
reasoningEn: The source identifies the underlying lesion of IgA vasculitis as leukocytoclastic small-vessel vasculitis with IgA deposition.
incorrectOptionsAr: Thrombocytopenia ليست سبب الـpurpura في IgA vasculitis؛ من شروط الصورة الكلاسيكية أن تكون palpable purpura بدون thrombocytopenia أو coagulopathy.
clinicalPearl: IgA vasculitis = nonthrombocytopenic palpable purpura plus variable joint, GI, and renal involvement.

sourceRefs.notes: Also recalled 2021; source explanation cites UpToDate.

topic: Vasculitis and other Conditions Associated with Hematuria
stemEn: A child presented with the shown skin lesions. He also complains of ankle and abdominal pain, consistent with Henoch-Schonlein purpura (IgA vasculitis). Which of the following is correct regarding this diagnosis?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار skin biopsy لأنه في الحالات غير المكتملة أو غير المعتادة يمكن إظهار leukocytoclastic vasculitis مع predominant IgA deposition. لكنه يذكر أيضًا أن التشخيص غالبًا clinical ولا يحتاج biopsy في كل حالة نموذجية، لذلك صياغة 'will confirm' تحتاج تحقق قبل النشر النهائي.
reasoningEn: The source key is skin biopsy, while its own explanation notes that typical IgA vasculitis is usually diagnosed clinically and biopsy is mainly supportive in incomplete or unusual cases.
incorrectOptionsAr: Intussusception complication معروفة لكنها ليست في معظم المرضى. Thrombocytopenia ليست جزءًا من HSP الكلاسيكي. Low IgA ليست finding تشخيصية متوقعة.
clinicalPearl: Typical IgA vasculitis is usually a clinical diagnosis; biopsy is most useful when the presentation is incomplete or atypical.
diagnosticSteps: Link the original rash image before publication
Consider biopsy if presentation is atypical or diagnosis uncertain

topic: Vasculitis and other Conditions Associated with Hematuria
stemEn: A child presented with a complaint consistent with Henoch-Schonlein purpura (IgA vasculitis). Which of the following is the most common complication associated with this disease?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار renal failure، لكنه في الشرح نفسه يقول إن kidney involvement يحدث في نحو 21–54% بينما impaired kidney function/renal failure يحدث في minority. لذلك مفتاح السؤال بصياغة 'most common complication' غير متسق مع الشرح ويجب ألا يُعتمد كverifiedAnswer قبل استرجاع wording/hints الأصلية.
reasoningEn: The source key is renal failure, but the source's own explanation says hematuria/kidney involvement is common whereas impaired kidney function is a minority finding, creating an internal inconsistency.
incorrectOptionsAr: TTP ليست complication نموذجية للـIgA vasculitis، لكن ذلك لا يجعل صياغة renal failure كـ'most common complication' موثوقة تلقائيًا.
clinicalPearl: Renal involvement is the key long-term prognostic issue in IgA vasculitis; most pediatric renal disease is mild, while severe renal failure is uncommon.
diagnosticSteps: Recover original exam wording if possible
Verify complication wording against current references

topic: Vasculitis and other Conditions Associated with Hematuria
stemEn: A child presented with swelling of the feet and wrist (arthritis), blue dots on the lower limbs, and mild abdominal pain. He has no ascites, consistent with Henoch-Schonlein purpura (IgA vasculitis). Which laboratory finding is most likely to be seen?
explanationAr: الـIgA vasculitis قد تصيب الكلى، وأكثر presentation شائع هو microscopic أو gross hematuria مع أو بدون proteinuria. لذلك المصدر يختار microscopic hematuria.
reasoningEn: Renal involvement in IgA vasculitis commonly manifests as microscopic hematuria.
incorrectOptionsAr: بقية الخيارات غير محفوظة في المصدر، لذلك لم تُختلق distractors جديدة.
clinicalPearl: Urinalysis is essential in IgA vasculitis even when the child has no urinary symptoms.

topic: Vasculitis and other Conditions Associated with Hematuria
stemEn: A picture showed legs with purpura, consistent with Henoch-Schonlein purpura (IgA vasculitis). What is your plan after discharge?

options.text: Follow up with blood pressure measurement and urine analysis

explanationAr: بسبب احتمال ظهور renal involvement بعد البداية، المصدر يوصي بمتابعة blood pressure وurinalysis بعد الخروج؛ معظم الأطفال الذين سيطورون nephritis يظهر ذلك خلال الأشهر الأولى.
reasoningEn: The source recommends serial urinalysis and blood-pressure monitoring because renal involvement may appear after the initial IgA vasculitis presentation.
incorrectOptionsAr: عدم المتابعة غير مناسب لأن renal disease قد تكون initially silent وتظهر لاحقًا.
clinicalPearl: Renal surveillance after IgA vasculitis is important even if the initial urinalysis is normal.

topic: Vasculitis and other Conditions Associated with Hematuria
stemEn: A patient developed acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis two weeks after impetigo. Which antibody titer is most likely to be identified?

options.text: Antibodies to deoxyribonuclease B (DNase B antibody)

explanationAr: بعد streptococcal skin infection/impetigo يكون anti-DNase B أكثر فائدة من ASO؛ لذلك المصدر يختار DNase B antibody. ASO يكون أكثر شيوعًا بعد streptococcal pharyngitis.
reasoningEn: Anti-DNase B is the source's preferred serologic evidence of recent streptococcal skin infection preceding APSGN.
incorrectOptionsAr: ASO قد لا يرتفع بشكل موثوق بعد skin infection مقارنةً بـanti-DNase B. ANA لا يثبت antecedent streptococcal infection ويُستخدم في autoimmune workup.
clinicalPearl: For APSGN after impetigo, anti-DNase B is generally more useful than ASO for documenting recent streptococcal infection.
diagnosticSteps: Assess complement and renal function as clinically indicated
Document recent streptococcal infection with appropriate serology
